dedupe_keys.name: hip hydrologisk informations og prognosesystem danish near surface groundwater streamflow and sea level data and model forecasts

description: HIP, the Hydrological Information and Prediction system, gives shared access to data and model results on the near-surface water cycle in Denmark and how climate change will affect it. The documentation read on 2026-09-28 says HIP shows measurements of near-surface groundwater, streamflow and sea level pulled by API from the data owners, from the early 1900s to the latest readings, and national model results from GEUS's National Water Resources Model, a three-dimensional physically based model, as a daily 100 m grid for a historical period up to today with 10-day forecasts, and for 2041-2070 and 2071-2100 based on DMI climate scenarios under RCP 4.5 and RCP 8.5; depth to groundwater can be shown by day, month, season or year, and support maps such as daily updated stream centrelines and catchments come with WMS, WFS and download. Coverage is national. Access is free through the viewer, API and web services; the licence is not stated in the documentation read. Caveats: model results carry uncertainty at local scale, and measurements belong to many owners with their own quality checks. It supports groundwater and fluvial flood exposure studies of buildings, roads and drainage under climate change. Related records: data-kamp-denmark-climate-adaptation-land-use-tool and data-denmark-high-water-statistics-2024 complement it.
